topic: Auto-expiry alerts for work permits and visas — how the dashboard surfaces renewals 30/60/90 days out
format: Lead with a quote or question from a customer, then explain the feature built in response
post:
One expired visa. One border checkpoint. One project stopped cold.

That's the message an HR manager at a Muscat trading company sent us. By the time she reached out, the damage was already done — travel blocked, project delayed, emergency filing fees paid.

The permit had been sitting in a spreadsheet nobody opened.

This is exactly why SmartPRO Hub built auto-expiry alerts. The dashboard flags every work permit and visa at 90, 60, and 30 days before expiry — no manual tracking, no one has to remember to check.

HR managers get the full workforce picture in one view: who's expiring this month, who's coming up next quarter, what's already moving through the renewal queue.

No spreadsheets. No WhatsApp reminder chains. No checkpoint surprises.

For companies managing 50 or 200+ employees across Oman and the GCC, this is the gap between catching a renewal in time and scrambling to fix it after. The cost difference between those two scenarios can be significant — in fees, delays, and the kind of stress nobody budgets for.

The tracking is built into the same platform handling WPS payroll, Omanization quotas, and Ministry of Labour filings. Not a separate tool. Not another login.

One missed renewal can ground a project. Staying on top of it shouldn't require a dedicated person doing nothing else.
